document.title: Handling guidance for model-detected surface defects on hot-rolled flat steel
document.drafted_by: AI-assisted draft from public sources; not reviewed
document.scope: Hot-rolled steel plates and wide flats, delivered under EN 10163-2. Not valid for sections, cold-rolled, coated or stainless products without separate review.
document.ordered_surface_class: SET PER ORDER: EN 10163-2 class A or B, subclass 1, 2 or 3
rules: Only entries with status 'approved' may be shown to users as guidance.
A model detection is not a confirmed defect. Every entry starts with visual confirmation on the material.
Accept, repair or reject decisions need depth and affected-area measurements the model does not provide. They are made by an authorised inspector against the ordered EN 10163 class.
Do not copy text from paid standards into this file. Reference document and section only.

SCI-GN-3.05.citation: SteelConstruction.info Guidance Note No. 3.05, Surface defects on steel materials (summary of BS EN 10163)

VDEH-ATLAS-HR.citation: VDEh (ed.), Surface Defects in Hot Rolled Flat Steel Products, 2nd edition, Verlag Stahleisen, Duesseldorf
VDEH-ATLAS-HR.access: Only the defect list with short definitions was read. Full entries (photos, causes) not read. Copyright of the online scan unclear; buy from Stahleisen before relying on it.

JANSTO-2012.citation: Jansto, S.G.; Stalheim, D.G. Hot Rolling Surface Quality Issues. 49th ABM Rolling Seminar, Rio de Janeiro, 2012, pp. 405-416. DOI 10.5151/2594-5297-22581
sections_used: 2 Hot rolling induced surface quality defects
JANSTO-2012.access: Free. Only abstract and an excerpt were read; corrective actions in the body have NOT been extracted. Reviewer should read it.

steps: 1. Confirm on the material that the detected area is a real surface discontinuity, not illumination, residual scale texture or a model error.
2. Measure the depth and the affected area of the discontinuity.
3. Compare with the limits for the ordered EN 10163-2 class. Within limits it is an imperfection and may remain; beyond limits, or extensive, it is a defect and must be repaired.
4. Repair defects by chipping and/or grinding. Weld repair only if the ordered subclass allows it: subclass 1 permitted, subclass 2 only if agreed at order, subclass 3 not allowed.
5. Check the remaining thickness after repair. Class B: never below the minimum thickness of the tolerance standard EN 10029.
6. Record the measurement, decision and inspector in the inspection record. Material that cannot be repaired within the rules is rejected by the authorised inspector, not by this system.

Crazing.mapping_confidence: medium: same name, but NEU-DET gives no definition; metallurgist to confirm
Crazing.definition: Network of fine cracks, sometimes hair cracks, caused by weakened grain boundaries.
Crazing.typical_causes_note: Not extracted from a read source. Reviewer to add from VDEh atlas section 3.3 full entry.
class_specific_handling: If confirmed as cracks: under EN 10163-2 class A, cracks are always defects regardless of depth and must be repaired (common steps 4-6).

Inclusion.mapped_term: Shell (VDEh 2.1) or seams (VDEh 2.2): laps or stripes containing non-metallic inclusions
Inclusion.mapping_confidence: low: NEU-DET 'inclusion' has no published definition; two possible mappings
Inclusion.definition: Surface discontinuity containing non-metallic material: irregular laps (shell) or stripes along the rolling direction (seams).
typical_causes: Non-metallic inclusions originating before rolling (steelmaking or casting stage) [VDEH-ATLAS-HR 2.1, 2.2 short definitions]
class_specific_handling: If confirmed as shell or seam: under EN 10163-2 class A these are always defects and must be repaired (common steps 4-6).
Report to the steel supplier when confirmed; origin is upstream of the inspection point.

Patches.mapping_confidence: none: no matching term found in EN 10163 summary or VDEh atlas list. Candidates seen: 'patch-like' shell (VDEh 2.1), 'sand patches' (SCI-GN-3.05). Neither confirmed.

Pitted surface.mapped_term: Pitting (VDEh 1.2), longitudinal pitting (VDEh 9.1) or corrosion pitting
Pitted surface.mapping_confidence: low: three possible origins with different handling
Pitted surface.definition: Small depressions or open voids distributed over the surface.
typical_causes: Broken-open gas inclusions near the surface [VDEH-ATLAS-HR 1.2]
Stock particles welded onto work rolls and printed onto the product [VDEH-ATLAS-HR 9.1]
Rusting during storage; covered separately in SCI GN 8.01 [SCI-GN-3.05 scope]
class_specific_handling: Identify which origin applies before choosing a corrective action; handling of the material itself follows common steps 2-6.

Rolled-in scale.mapped_term: Rolled-in primary scale (VDEh 5.1) or rolled-in secondary scale (VDEh 5.2)
Rolled-in scale.mapping_confidence: high: same term in VDEh atlas and EN 10163 summary
Rolled-in scale.definition: Oxide scale pressed into the surface during hot rolling.
typical_causes: Primary: furnace or roughing-mill scale that was not fully removed before rolling [VDEH-ATLAS-HR 5.1]
Secondary: scale not fully removed and rolled in within the finishing train [VDEH-ATLAS-HR 5.2]
Rolled-in scale.context: Reported as the most frequent surface quality issue in structural plate and coil hot rolling [JANSTO-2012 2.1].
class_specific_handling: Process: report primary vs secondary to the rolling mill; corrective actions to be added by reviewer from JANSTO-2012 body.

Scratches.mapping_confidence: high: same term in VDEh atlas and EN 10163 summary
Scratches.definition: Mechanical surface damage of varying severity, usually linear.
typical_causes: Mechanical handling; reported as the third most frequent hot-rolling surface issue [JANSTO-2012 2]
class_specific_handling: Process: check handling and transport equipment along the line; specific actions to be added by reviewer.
